items.description: The foundational text on discrete choice modeling in transportation. Developed the random utility framework that underpins modern mode choice and demand forecasting.

items.description: Introduces market share inversion mapping observed shares to mean utilities, enabling IV estimation with aggregate data.

rows.title: Essential Staggered Treatment Timing Toolkit
rows.description: Core packages for causal inference work

items.name: csdid
items.description: Python adaptation of the R `did` package. Implements multi-period DiD with staggered treatment timing (Callaway & Sant’Anna).

items.name: bacondecomp
items.description: Performs Goodman-Bacon decomposition showing how two-way fixed effects (TWFE) estimates are weighted averages of all possible 2×2 DiD comparisons. Essential for diagnosing negative weights problems in staggered adoption designs.

items.name: did
items.description: Implements group-time average treatment effects (ATT(g,t)) for staggered DiD designs with multiple periods and variation in treatment timing. Provides flexible aggregation into event-study plots or overall treatment effect estimates, addressing the well-documented negative weighting issues with conventional TWFE under staggered adoption.

items.name: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (ResNet)
items.description: ResNet architecture enabling powerful visual features for image clustering.

items.name: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
items.category: Statistics > Multiple Testing & False Discovery Rate
items.description: One of the most-cited statistics papers ever (~100,000 citations). Introduced FDR as alternative to FWER—controls expected proportion of false discoveries among rejections. The BH step-up procedure is now default in experimentation platforms at Google, Netflix, Meta. Essential when testing 500 experiments or 20 metrics per A/B test.

rows.title: Learning Path: From OLS to Causal Forests
rows.description: A learning journey from basic regression to cutting-edge causal ML

items.name: Mostly Harmless Econometrics
items.description: THE bible of applied econometrics. Covers regression, IV, DiD, and RDD with focus on clean identification. Nobel laureate Angrist's practical guide to credible causal inference.

items.name: Regression Models and Life Tables
items.description: The Cox proportional hazards model—one of the most cited statistical methods ever. Foundation for survival analysis across oncology, cardiology, and reliability.

items.name: Hedonic Prices and Implicit Markets: Product Differentiation in Pure Competition
items.description: Theoretical foundation for all hedonic pricing models; every AVM derives from this framework.

items.name: What Drives Media Slant? Evidence from U.S. Daily Newspapers
items.category: Choice Models & Dynamic Choice > Discrete Choice (Logit, Mixed Logit)
items.description: Discrete choice demand model incorporating ideological content; demonstrates how consumer preferences drive product differentiation in information markets.

items.name: Product Differentiation, Search Costs, and Competition in the Mutual Fund Industry: A Case Study of S&P 500 Index Funds
items.category: Choice Models & Dynamic Choice > Consideration Sets & Attention
items.description: Models search frictions for financially homogeneous products; explains fund proliferation and fee dispersion via information costs.

items.name: Nonparametric Estimation from Incomplete Observations
items.description: Introduced the Kaplan-Meier estimator (product-limit estimator), the universal method for estimating survival curves from censored data. Every survival analysis begins here—essential for visualizing retention curves, comparing cohorts, and calculating median time-to-churn.

items.name: Regression Models and Life-Tables
items.description: Introduced the Cox proportional hazards model, enabling regression analysis on survival data while leaving the baseline hazard unspecified. Ranked 24th among all scientific papers ever published. The workhorse for identifying churn drivers and estimating treatment effects of retention interventions.
